messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: canary-eu-1 experienced 5xx spike. 5xx rate: 8% (baseline 0.2%), p50 latency 220ms -> 920ms. Traffic split: 5% canary. Trigger: /metrics/canary/5xx. Severity: P2.
Maria (on-call): I'm on it. Paging @Ethan SRE and @Sam SRE. Any recent deploys to canary-eu-1?
Ethan SRE: saw the deploy ~4m ago from release pipeline, single commit: a1b2c3d (routing change). Rolling 5% traffic to new-routing flag.
Sam SRE: Confirmed increased 5xx from the routerlayer. Stack traces look like: `InvalidEdgeKeyError` in route_selection.
Dave (release): that commit was the one-line change to prefer fragment-based routing for long prompts. Rolling it to canary only.
Maria (on-call): Ok step 1: kill the feature flag to stop routing to the new path. If 5xx persists, we'll revert the commit. I'll flip flag now.
Maria (on-call): `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_TOKEN' https://flags.internal/api/flags/new-routing/kill` -> 202 Accepted :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sam SRE: flag flip acknowledged by flag-service. Metrics showed small drop but still elevated. 5xx at 6% now.
Ethan SRE: I'll look at logs. Running `kubectl logs -n canary svc/router-eu-1 --since=5m | grep InvalidEdgeKeyError`
Ethan SRE: I see a surge of `InvalidEdgeKeyError` from shard-7 only. Could be a sharding mismatch with the new routing.
Karen (prod-eng): If it's shard-specific, we should stop traffic to that shard quickly. Can we remove shard-7 from the canary pool?
Sam SRE: We can temporarily take shard-7 out of balancer. Running: `servicectl pool remove router-eu-1 shard-7 --reason "canary instability"`
Sam SRE: Removed shard-7. Observability: 5xx down to 1.2% within 90s.
Maria (on-call): Nice. Customer impact? CS Ops, any hits?
CS Ops: We've got 23 distinct customer requests failed in last 10m, mostly non-paid sandbox. No major customers showing alerts yet. We're preemptively drafting a note.
Ethan SRE: Given the shard removal and flag kill helped, I'd still prefer we revert the single commit a1b2c3d to remove risk. Dave, can you coordinate a single-commit revert + canary redeploy?
Dave (release): On it. Preparing revert PR: `git revert --no-edit a1b2c3d` -> PR #4321. Running CI now. ETA for patch deploy ~8-10m if green.
Maria (on-call): Make it a hotfix job. We want minimal churn: revert -> canary -> monitor -> promote. Keep traffic at 5% canary.
Dave (release): CI passed. Deploying hotfix: `releasectl deploy --env canary-eu-1 --tag revert-a1b2c3d --notes "hotfix: revert routing change"`
incident-bot: Deploy started for canary-eu-1 (revert-a1b2c3d). Commit: revert-a1b2c3d. Pipeline: canary->wait->promote.
Sam SRE: Rollout complete to canary. Running verification scripts.
Sam SRE: Verification: synthetic requests show 0.0% 5xx over last 2m, p50 latency back to 210ms.
Maria (on-call): Monitoring dashboards look stable. 5xx now steady at 0.15%.
CS Ops: Sent short note to affected sandbox customers: "We observed errors affecting a small set of sandbox requests. A fix has been deployed to canary and we're monitoring. No action required from customers"
Ethan SRE: I'm going to run a quick grep across edge configs to ensure no stale references to the new-routing flag remain: `rg "new-routing" infra/ || true`
Ethan SRE: No other uses found. Good.
Karen (prod-eng): Follow-up: we should add a unit test for shard selection when routing key unavailable. Filing ticket.
Maria (on-call): Agreed. Please tag me in the ticket.
Dave (release): Will plan a controlled promotion to prod in 30m once canary stable for 20m.
Maria (on-call): Handoff: I'm on-call for another 40m then handing to @Ethan SRE. I'll annotate the incident in the runbook.
Sam SRE: Addendum: we've saved the balancer config that removed shard-7, and restored it after revert. No persistent config drift.
Maria (on-call): Closing note: root cause appears to be routing logic change in a1b2c3d that didn't account for rare edge keys (shard-7). Mitigation: killed flag + removed shard + revert. Postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=resolved (mitigation applied). Incident ID: INC-2026-0892.
Maria (on-call): Thanks all. Good coordination. CS Ops — please update customers if anything else pops up.
CS Ops: Will do. Leaving thread open for postmortem links and follow-ups.
